paper.title: Fixed Confidence and Fixed Tolerance Bi-level Optimization for Selecting the Best Optimized System

settings.name_in_paper: FCFT bi-level optimization for selecting the best optimized system
unmapped: Bi-level structure: each system k's performance h(k, x_k*) depends on a continuous decision variable x_k* that minimizes a separate lower-level stochastic objective f(k, .), solved by stochastic gradient (SAGD/SGD) queries
Learner has two oracles: stochastic gradients of F(k,x,xi) and noisy evaluations H(k,x,zeta)
Function evaluations across systems are jointly multivariate normal with unknown covariance (common random numbers allowed)
The learner knows the strong convexity mu_k, Lipschitz constants L_k, sub-Gaussian gradient noise sigma_G, domain diameter D, and smoothness constants nu_k, M_k used to set SAGD iteration counts
settings.definition_quote: with probability at least $1-\alpha$, find $\bar{k}$ such that $$ h(\Bar{k}, x_{\Bar{k}}^*) \le  h(k^*,x^*_{k^*}) + \epsilon,$$ where $\epsilon>0$ represents the error tolerance of the decision maker.

settings.name_in_paper: Lower-level stochastic optimization of a single system by SGD (same upper and lower objective)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Stochastic first-order optimization of a single system (not a bandit problem); the guarantee holds under an assumed asymptotic limiting distribution
unmapped: Stochastic gradients with bounded (2+eps) moments and continuous covariance; f three-times continuously differentiable
The learner knows mu, ||Cov(G(x*,xi))||_2, and ||Hessian f(x*)||_2 (or upper bounds on them)
settings.definition_quote: Suppose $ N(f(x_{N}) - f(x^*)) \sim Z^\intercal \nabla^2 f(x^*) Z $, where $Z \sim \mathcal{N} \left(0, \Sigma_{\infty} \right)$.

algorithms.name: Multi-stage Pruning-Optimization Framework (with Fully Sequential Pruning and SAGD Optimization)
Optimization (Asymptotic) via SGD with step size gamma/l

conditions: Assumption 5: f(k,.) satisfies smoothness-type inequality with nu_k, M_k; F convex in x; unbiased sub-Gaussian stochastic gradients; bounded domain diameter D_k
Assumption 1: function evaluations jointly multivariate normal, i.i.d. across replications
f(k,.) mu_k-strongly convex and h(k,.) L_k-Lipschitz (Assumption 2, used in the Optimization step)
Optimization step uses the non-asymptotic SAGD approach (Algorithm 3)
tuning: alpha_t = alpha/(2T) split between optimization and pruning

source.label: thm: statistical validity
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions \ref{assump: convex} and \ref{assump: prunning} hold. Then, with probability at least $1-\alpha$, Algorithm \ref{alg: RSCOP} outputs an $\epsilon$-optimal system.

results.notes: The guarantee is delta-PAC correctness: the probability of not returning an epsilon-optimal system is at most alpha (the paper's alpha is delta). There is no formal sample-complexity bound. The order N^t = O(log^2(T/alpha)/eps_t^4) appears only in the text, where T is the number of stages rather than a horizon.

symbols.b: gamma^2/(2 gamma mu - 1) * ||Cov(G(x*,xi))||_2 * ||Hessian f(x*)||_2; equals ||Cov||_2 ||Hessian||_2 / mu^2 at gamma = 1/mu
symbols.gamma: SGD step-size constant (step gamma/l), gamma > 1/(2 mu)

conditions: Assumes N(f(x_N) - f(x*)) is exactly distributed as Z^T Hessian f(x*) Z with Z ~ N(0, Sigma_infty), i.e. the asymptotic limit of Theorem 2

source.label: thm: quadratic normal concentration
source.quote: Suppose $ N(f(x_{N}) - f(x^*)) \sim Z^\intercal \nabla^2 f(x^*) Z $, where $Z \sim \mathcal{N} \left(0, \Sigma_{\infty} \right)$. Then,  if we set $N^t$ to be $\min\{N: N\ge \frac{b}{\epsilon_t} \max\{[4\log\frac{1}{\alpha_t}+\frac{3d}{2}], 2d \} \}$, we have $\mathbb{P}( f(x_{N^t}) - f(x^*) > \epsilon_t ) \le \alpha_t$...

results.notes: Number of SGD iterations needed to reach f(x_N) - f(x*) <= epsilon_t with probability 1 - alpha_t, where alpha_t is mapped to delta. The result is only asymptotically valid because it assumes the limiting distribution holds exactly.
